bleachedEventDetails:
Join us for a hands-on, practical workshop designed to equip teachers with the knowledge and resources to successfully implement RoboCup Junior in your school.

This session will go through the four RoboCup competition divisions:

OnStage – Creative robotics meets performance. Learn how students combine coding, robotics and storytelling to produce engaging live performances.

Rescue Line – Develop autonomous robots that follow lines, navigate obstacles, and complete simulated rescue missions.

Rescue Maze – Explore advanced navigation using sensors, mapping, and problem-solving to simulate disaster rescue environments.

Soccer – Program and build robots capable of playing fully autonomous robotic soccer.

Participants will:
-Gain an overview of competition rules and structures
-Explore hardware options (including classroom-friendly platforms)
-Programming strategies and sensor integration
-Discuss classroom implementation, assessment ideas, and team preparation
-Receive practical tips to prepare for the RoboCup events and competitions

Details: Saturday 7th March, 1pm - 4pm
Location: Melrose Park Public School (110 Wharf Road West Ryde NSW) https://maps.app.goo.gl/6r7wEUdcxSARBfJS9 Enter via Mary St entrance.
Registration Fee: $0
Direct Inquiries to: Pam Grover pam.grover@robocupjunior.org.au

name: Maitland Region - RoboCup Junior Workshop
bleachedEventDetails:
Maitland Region RoboCup Junior Workshop

Join us for an intensive, hands-on robotics development day designed to kickstart your school’s journey into the RoboCup Junior Australia Rescue competition. This workshop is specifically tailored for students and teachers in the Maitland and surrounding Hunter areas.

Event Overview

Rutherford Technology High School

Venue: Rutherford Technology High School, 30 Avery St, Rutherford NSW 2320.

Date: Wednesday, June 3rd, 2026.

Time: 9:30 AM – 2:30 PM (Approx.).

Cost: Free (Industry sponsored by 4Tel and 4AI Systems).

What to Expect
This full-day session focuses on the Rescue (Line) category. Participants will learn to build and program autonomous robots capable of navigating complex paths and simulated disaster scenarios.

Line Following Fundamentals: Mastering sensor calibration and logic to handle sharp turns and gaps.

Advanced Control: Introduction to Proportional (P) control for smoother, faster navigation.

Obstacle Management: Using ultrasonic sensors to identify and bypass "debris" in the rescue zone.

Competition Preparation: Direct insights into scoring and rules for the upcoming Hunter Region competition in July.

Hardware & Equipment
Provided: LEGO SPIKE Prime kits will be available for all teams to use on the day.

Bring Your Own: We highly encourage visiting schools and students to bring their own robotics platforms (SPIKE Prime, EV3, or Arduino) to ensure they can continue their development back at their own campuses.

Calling All Surrounding Schools
We invite schools from across the Maitland, Cessnock, and Singleton areas to participate. This is a collaborative environment where students can learn from one another and from world-class industry experts.

Led by Industry Excellence
The workshop is delivered by Dr. Aaron Wong, AI Engineering Manager at 4AI Systems and a 2008 RoboCup World Champion. Dr. Wong brings over a decade of experience in high-level robotics, academic research in neuroscience, and industrial AI application to the classroom.

Register your interest now to secure a spot for your team!

This event is supported by RoboCup Junior Hunter Region, RoboCup Junior NSW, and 4AI Systems

bleachedEventDetails: This year, we are running a Sydney Regional competition at the start of Term 3, at Thomas Hassall Anglican College. • Location: Thomas Hassall Anglican College. Rawdon Middleton VC Sports Complex – Flynn Ave, Middleton Grange NSW • Parking is available onsite via the entrance on Flynn Ave. • Time: 9.00 - 12.00 (preparation /workshop time), 12.00 - 3.00 (compete against other teams) • Cost: $30 per team • Audience: open to school and community-based teams. Experienced facilitators will be available throughout the session to offer guidance, answer questions and support teams as they prepare for competition. • A canteen is available on site. name: State Competition
bleachedEventDetails: The NSW RoboCup Junior State Competition is back, bringing together the brightest young minds in robotics from across New South Wales. Join us on August 24th and 25th at the Whitlam Leisure Centre for two days of competition and creativity. Information pack: https://rcja.my.canva.site/nsw-state-2026 Risk assessment: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qIXhvdO3gUQYpUe7CJfjfDi8U6pUH23tn3ucwJkqn4U/edit?usp=sharing Day 1: Rescue - Riley Rover & Primary OnStage - Primary Novice, Ollie Onstage Soccer - Simple Simon & Standard League Maze - Mighty Maisy Maze Day 2: Rescue - Secondary, Open OnStage - Primary Novice, Secondary Novice, Open Soccer - Lightweight & Open Maze - Intermediate & Open *Please note that Primary OnStage will be run over both days. You will need to select one day to attend when registering. All students attending must be registered. Mentors must be in receipt of Participation Deeds prior to registering students for the event, and submit these for all registered students on the event day. All mentors must submit a Mentor Declaration on the event day. Participation Deeds and Mentor Declarations can be downloaded from the compliance forms section of our website. Riley rover divisions on Day 2 may be available by request. --- Ollie Onstage is a new NSW exclusive OnStage Novice division designed for primary students, where no team members have previously participated in OnStage. Each performance must use only one student-built robot. Participation in this competition counts as one year of the two years allowed for students in the OnStage Novice division. The rules and marking grids for OnStage Novice will be applied.
